A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VITA. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison. Reformatting, relocation, and renumbering can be resolved without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulation and real-world robot experiments, efficiency measurements, ablations, and robustness evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds a reported one-step MeanFlow experiment on PushT in Appendix E.3.

M1.justification: v4 Appendix E.3 adds a MeanFlow-based one-step adaptation of VITA. The default six-step OT-CFM procedure, architecture, action autoencoder, and FLD/FLC objectives remain unchanged; the adaptation does not replace the main method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine simulated and five real-world tasks, including the retained perturbation and unseen-object scenarios. The new one-step experiment uses the existing PushT task without expanding data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a comparison between a MeanFlow-based one-step VITA variant and the default six-step configuration. The existing FM, DP, ACT, and architecture comparator sets remain unchanged. MP1 and Consistency Models receive citations but no separate reported evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated simulation evaluation interval from every 500 training steps to every 200. This establishes a reported protocol revision, not that experiments were rerun. Appendix E.3 also introduces evaluation of one-step generation alongside the retained six-step configuration.

E4.justification: The new Appendix E.3 investigates the speed–success tradeoff of integrating one-step MeanFlow. Existing loss, frozen-autoencoder, stochasticity, architecture, hyperparameter, failure-case, perturbation, and generalization analyses are retained; the latent-collapse discussion moves from B.6.3 to B.11.

E5.justification: Both retain means and standard deviations over three seeds in Table 2 and three-seed uncertainty bands in Figure 16. The new one-step result introduces no additional run-count, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: All retained table values and figure results match after relocation and renumbering. Appendix E.3 newly reports approximately 2× faster inference and 74% PushT success for the MeanFlow adaptation, compared with the retained 88% default result. This is a different-method comparison, not deterioration of unchanged VITA.

T1.justification: The flow formulation, learning-loss definitions, decoder assumption, FLD/FLC equivalence theorem, and Appendix A lemma, proofs, and corollaries are retained. The added MeanFlow discussion supplies no new mathematical derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The central noise-free policy, FLD, lightweight architecture, and efficiency claims remain. The conclusion newly suggests FLD could apply to other generative tasks and latent-action policies. Appendix C adds a novelty assertion that VITA is the first policy jointly learning flow matching and latent actions end to end.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendix B.6.1 expand the explanation that aligned visual/action latents make incremental refinement feasible with MLPs. Appendix B.8.2 adds an argument about precision relative to multimodality, while E.3 identifies reduced success as a limitation of further one-step acceleration.

D1.justification: The new reproducibility statement describes accompanying training scripts, evaluation pipelines, and configuration files; v3 advertises code, datasets, and demos more generally. The project-page destination, hardware information, and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. This expands documented resource information without establishing a new release.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to MeanFlow, MP1, Consistency Models, and Pan et al.'s analysis of generative robotic control, supporting limited discussion of one-step generation and multimodality. Appendix C adds the joint end-to-end learning novelty assertion. The existing DSD comparison is relocated rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the encoder description and latent-action terminology, expand Section 5.4, and revise the conclusion. v4 adds ethics, reproducibility, and acknowledgements sections and relocates the latent-collapse discussion. Most prose and the main scientific section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document-wide ICLR conversion redesigns the title page, headers, typography, margins, and display sizing and placement. Figure 1 moves onto the first page, and v3 Table 4 moves into Appendix D.2.1 as Table 7. Figure artwork and table structures are retained, while Figure 7's caption is rewritten.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful evidence about the limits of faster generation: Appendix E.3 reports roughly 2× acceleration with 74% rather than 88% PushT success. Expanded explanations also clarify the rationale for lightweight MLPs. These gains are limited by sparse settings and uncertainty information for the new variant and the unexplained evaluation-interval revision; the main empirical and theoretical evidence remains unchanged.
